Subject: POC preflight: scope, success criteria, resources

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we draft the POC playbook:

Summary of what we heard
- Goal: Validate automated ticket classification + suggested responses for 6 high-volume intents (billing, password reset, order status, returns, shipping exceptions, fournisseur updates).
- Success criteria (customer-facing): 80% intent classification accuracy on sampled production traffic; median end-to-end latency <200ms for 95th percentile; two-week time-to-value where Starlane ops can route suggestions to agents.
- Data: Starlane will provide a month of anonymized ticket samples (S3 link) + 1K hand-labeled examples for bootstrapping.

Proposed POC scope & milestones
1) Week 0 (Prep) — ingress access, sample extract, security checklist done.
2) Week 1 — baseline model + initial mapping to your intents; daily checkpoints.
3) Week 2 — closed-loop suggestions in sandbox; evaluation against held-out labels and fast feedback.

Ownership (please confirm):
- Redwood: Jordan (technical lead), Ben (inference/config), Marissa (customer ops & rollout).
- Starlane: Alex (product sponsor), Procurement (commercial), an engineer for data access (TBD).

Immediate asks for this week
- Alex: confirm the data S3 path and the engineer to grant access.
- Procurement: confirm NDA/PO cadence — if you need a formal approval we can push a short form NDA via DocuSign.
- Starlane ops: confirm 3–4 sample intents to prioritize (your call earlier suggested billing, returns, shipping).

I attached a short POC scope doc (poc-scope-v1.pdf) and put a working copy in Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cPOCPlan

If we lock these items by EOD Friday, we can kick off prep work Monday and aim for an end-of-week demo. Do those dates work for you?

Best,
